<thought>The spectrum shows a classic carbon isotopic pattern: a dominant M peak, an M+1 peak at ~10 % (consistent with ~10–12 carbons), and progressively smaller M+2, M+3, etc., spaced by ~1.003 Da. No large M+2 peaks characteristic of Cl, Br, or S are present, and the minor higher‑order peaks are consistent with additional 13C contributions rather than other elements. Thus, carbon is the only element that can be definitively identified from the isotopic distribution.</thought>
<final_answer>['C']</final_answer>
